doc.title: Luther Henderson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Harlem addresses and Sugar Hill
summary: He lists the places he lived in Harlem, ending on Sugar Hill, and dates the moves to the late 1920s and Evander Childs High School.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Before we get into that, tell me exactly when you, where you moved to in New York. Where did you live?

Where did I live? My first address in New York was 203 West 120th Street. And don't ask me how I remember that! Because we moved a lot of different places. And the next one that I remember was on what they now call, used to call, Strivers Row on 139th Street between 7th and 8th Avenues. And for a while, I remember 204 Seventh Avenue because that was there also, big place was there. I've lived in lots of different places in New York. The biggest portion of my growing up came on what we called Sugar Hill, I guess, because we lived at 80 St. Nicholas Place and 79 and … various places up there and that was the venue for my business with block gangs. We'd all get out in the back yard and play stick ball. At least they all did; I didn't, I wasn't so good at that, you know. But anyway.
We're talking around the period of 1924, '25 when you're first come in to New York?

Uh, that's with, yeah, '24, '25. I guess we would talk about the next 3 or 4 years 'cause I seem to remember that by the time we moved up to the Hill, it must have been a matter of maybe 4 or 5 years. I don't remember exactly, but it seems to me that … um … my sister … was … her first job, got a job teaching in Texas … and I think we were up on the Hill by the mid-'30s. I know that we were certainly there before that because in 1935 I graduated from Evander Child's High School and I'd been there four
years. So we had to be there by the '30s, 1930s. Yes, I did four years there, so I suspect that we moved there to that section around 1929, '30.
